\section{Resource conditions and recorded usage}
\label{app:resources}
The following tables account for recorded usage; they do not estimate rankings under equal resources. Each method has 30 episodes (ten per task). The query-4 rows describe prefixes of a 32-query task, not runs instructed to stop at four. The open-ended query-32 row continues its query-4 episodes and must not be added to that row.
\subsection{Surrogate and CFD requests}
Table~\ref{tab:resource-queries} separates prior information, online requests, private recommendation grades, and actual surrogate usage. The four surrogate-assisted baselines receive the same 62 development records; agents receive SuperWing source records but not this 62-record context. SMAC3 has neither the warm start nor surrogate access. Private grades are not returned to the method. They are additional recorded requests, not necessarily new solver executions.

The archive methods spend all 4,096 surrogate evaluations before online CFD; the adaptive baseline methods have spent 512 at query 4 and 4,096 at query 32. Agents choose their own usage. Agent counts sum committed ledger charges; exact repeats served from the episode cache are free and are excluded. Thus charged evaluations are not the number of tool invocations. Baseline counts come from checkpoint budget counters; SMAC3's zero follows from its CFD-only implementation. These accounting rules and the different information sets remain limitations of cross-family comparisons.
\subsection{Agent sessions and model usage}
Table~\ref{tab:resource-model} counts all launched sessions assigned to decisions through the checkpoint, including checkpoint-0 reviews, later reviews, reflection, errors and retries. Planning's nested model calls are included in its research sessions. Summed session elapsed time includes tool execution, local code, and waiting within sessions; it is neither pure model inference time nor end-to-end campaign wall time, and overlapping sessions need not be additive elapsed time. Token counts are provider-reported and incomplete for eleven sessions across the whole study. Cache-read tokens are reported separately. Dollar values are reference model charges, excluding CFD and hosting.

\subsection{CFD timing and unmeasured resources}
Table~\ref{tab:resource-cfd-time} uses the existing episode timing aggregates: summed mesh and flow-attempt wall seconds multiplied by 16 cores. These include online and private grading. They describe timing attached to evaluation records, not unique physical compute or a cloud bill: outcomes can be reused, some records have no timing, and the SMAC3 timing aggregate retains two superseded grades. The aggregates do not provide a separate query-4 timing total for the open-ended extension or the baselines. They also do not establish identical hardware across campaigns.

\begin{table}[htbp]\centering\scriptsize
\caption{CFD timing at each method's recorded final horizon. These rows cover different query horizons. No matched-runtime comparison is inferred.}
\label{tab:resource-cfd-time}
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}
\begin{tabular*}{\textwidth}{@{\extracolsep{\fill}}lrrr}\toprule
Method & Final query & Timed records & Recorded core-hours \\ \midrule
CMA-ES, no feedback & 32 & 1{,}123 & 16{,}689.1 \\
CMA-ES, selection only & 32 & 1{,}119 & 16{,}583.6 \\

Feedback-guided DE & 32 & 1{,}034 & 38{,}063.9 \\
SMAC3 & 32 & 954 & 35{,}306.8 \\
Open-ended research & 32 & 968 & 42{,}112.9 \\
Planning & 4 & 162 & 6{,}112.2 \\
Reflection & 4 & 167 & 6{,}391.6 \\
\bottomrule\end{tabular*}\end{table}

Optimizer CPU/GPU time, model-server compute, and consistent end-to-end episode wall time were not recorded across all methods. Missing values are not treated as zero. Consequently, neither equal CFD caps nor this accounting supplies a ranking under equal total computation or wall-clock limits. Such a ranking would require a new experiment with a common initial information set, resource rules and recommendation endpoint; it cannot be reconstructed by subtracting prior records or truncating costs after the fact.
\paragraph{Reproduction.} \texttt{analysis/20\_resource\_accounting.py} reads the released episode, evaluation and agent-session tables plus \texttt{data/surrogate\_usage.csv}, and writes per-episode and method-level tables and this appendix. The surrogate extract includes checkpoint counts for all 240 episodes and source fingerprints in \texttt{data/surrogate\_usage\_provenance.json}. The optional archive extractor is supplied separately; the original campaign archives are not required to reproduce the accounting tables.
